chains.title: From planning to the 1991 policy
steps: A mixed economy, with five year plans (Planning Commission, 1950)
IPR 1956 and licensing put the state in control of industry
Inward-looking trade: import substitution in the first seven plans
Loss-making public sector, permit licence raj, weak exports
The new economic policy of 1991

chains.title: How the Green Revolution fed the country
steps: HYV seeds for wheat and rice
Fertiliser, pesticide and regular water in correct proportions
A large increase in food grain production
Much grain is sold (marketed surplus); grain prices fall relatively
Low-income groups gain; the government builds a stock for shortages

chains.title: Land reforms: land to the tiller
steps: Intermediaries such as zamindars abolished
About 200 lakh tenants deal directly with the government
Tillers own land and keep the profit
An incentive to invest in improvements, if capital is available

chains.title: Land ceiling and how landlords escaped it
steps: Ceiling: a maximum size of land one person can own
Big landlords challenge the law in court, delaying it
They use the delay to register land in relatives' names
They escape the legislation and keep their land

chains.title: Why protect domestic industry?
steps: Young Indian industries can't yet compete with developed economies
Imports are restricted with tariffs and quotas
Domestic production replaces imports
Electronics and automobile industries develop under protection

chains.title: Box 2.6: how subsidies hide scarcity
steps: Water and electricity supplied free or subsidised
Prices no longer signal scarcity
They are used wastefully
Water-intensive crops grown where water is scarce
Scarce water resources are further depleted
